targets.review_note: Write the matrix as B+C*11^T with B=(1-C)I-C*U and U the strictly upper-triangular divisibility matrix. Solving B*h=1 gives h(i)=F(floor(N/i)) with F(x)=(1+C*sum_{d=2..x}F(floor(x/d)))/(1-C). The determinant lemma and the first component equation simplify det(A) to(1-C)^N*F(N). Memoize the distinct floor quotients and group equal quotients. For C=1, the last two rows coincide when N>=3; N1,2 both have determinant1. C=0 is the identity.

targets.review_note: Root at labeled vertex1. Every vertex has at most two children, exactly matching the stated degree limits. A bottom-up maximum matching greedily matches a root to one available child if there is one; the DP tracks matching size and whether the root remains available. One child contributes its choice of root label, while two unordered children require a binomial label split, both child-root choices, and division by2. Summing the two root states gives labeled trees with the required maximum matching, not the number of possible matchings.
